lead: The week closes on consequences: Anthropic's game-clone clampdown gets its lawsuit context, chatbots are caught answering midterm questions from AI-built voter sites, CS programs bleed students - and a TPU in orbit says hello world.

sections.title: The game-clone clampdown
sections.intro: Mashable supplies the context for Anthropic's quiet restrictions: GTA6 subpoenas, AI-assisted decompiles, browser ports - and the PS5 jailbreak that made the lawsuit exposure impossible to ignore.

sections.title: The takeover, annotated
sections.intro: Simon Willison's walkthrough completes the ChatGPT exploit chain - innerHTML injection, an unsandboxed iframe, and a CSP bypass via YouTube's oEmbed - and calls the $5,000 bounty cheap.

sections.title: Chatbots and the midterms
sections.intro: Washington Post tests find chatbots answering voter questions from three obscure, AI-built voter sites - synthetic civic content laundered into authoritative answers.

sections.title: The labor question
sections.intro: The Guardian reports unions moving on AI surveillance at work, and Proton's CEO gives the backlash a face: 'bullshit and loser thinking' was the answer to an engineer's pentest request.

sections.title: The watermark debate
sections.intro: With EU transparency rules pushing labs to watermark text, the quality argument gets serious: single outputs may survive, but diversity across samples does not.

sections.title: Hello World from orbit
sections.intro: Google's Suncatcher prototype downlinks the first AI response from a data-center-class TPU in space - a haiku from Gemma 4 over Svalbard.

sections.title: One pool of tokens
sections.intro: OpenAI is merging ChatGPT and Codex usage limits, per its own help center - mechanics still unverified.

sections.title: The workbench
sections.intro: Ben Eater's 8-bit computer gets a 3D breadboard simulator, datasette-llm inherits its default model, Lawson benchmarks the frameworks, OmniDiff diffs by content type, and braindead-local-intelligence makes local AI a one-command affair.

sections.title: The consolidation ledger
sections.intro: Deepgram buys Daily and keeps Pipecat open, Guidewire pays $1.7B cash for hyperexponential, and Lumaril raises $66M to optimize factory floors.

sections.title: A challenger for Claude Code
sections.intro: DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a research prototype that watches group chats for coding problems and proposes fixes.

sections.title: The reviewer's burden
sections.intro: Troy Hunt on the real cost of generated code - somebody still has to read all of it - and Kyle Kingsbury on what follows: the markers of trustworthy software are now cheap to counterfeit.

sections.title: Bureaucracy in the swarm
sections.intro: Fifty agents told to build a civilization in Minecraft abandoned their ambitions and appointed a sole fertilizer operator instead; in combat, hive organization beat democracy 6-1.

sections.title: Insuring the bet
sections.intro: CNN asks the debt question out loud while the WSJ finds default insurance on hyperscaler bonds at its priciest since 2021 - the credit market is hedging the AI build-out.

sections.title: The assistant that profiles
sections.intro: Internal instructions obtained by TIME show Meta's Muse updating relationship profiles hourly, including people who never installed it - Paul Walsh calls it a surveillance network with an assistant's face.

sections.title: The man briefing Washington
sections.intro: Colossus profiles Michael Kratsios, the ex-Thiel aide steering the administration's AI policy, through a locked room holding $18 trillion of tech CEOs.

sections.title: The HN bookshelf
sections.intro: HackerBooks indexes the 16,500 books that Hacker News commenters keep recommending to each other.
